prompt:
Create one professional detailed native PIXEL-ART animation SOURCE ATLAS of Uzi Doorman, exact selected incarnation: Murder Drones episode1 Pilot (2021), worker-drone Uzi before Solver forms.

CHARACTER APPEARANCE: Small worker robot, dark face screen with purple luminous eyes, short purple hair, purple knit cap and black hooded outfit, striped limbs and robot boots.
EXACT EQUIPMENT AND ROLE: Handmade long dark railgun with GREEN energy core.
SOURCE ACTION: Railgun d’Uzi. Brace the real handmade railgun, charge with a small contained green core and release from physical barrel col2 only; no Solver wings or red eyes.

Recognizable coherent clean16-bit game sprites, not photographs. Same design, scale, palette and physical limb/equipment count in ALL48drawings. Full complete bodies, feet, heads, clothing and full held weapons visible inside every cell. A naturally crouched figure must remain shorter, not stretched to the height of a standing pose. All figures face screen-right in the same three-quarter side-view. Neutral practical nonsexual game character presentation; non-graphic actions, no blood, gore, body damage or civilian targets.

STRICT GRID: exactly EIGHT COLUMNS by SIX ROWS = FORTY-EIGHT COMPLETE SEPARATE FIGURES. Landscape4:3 arrangement with square cells. All gutters generously transparent and empty. Transparent background, NO floor, ground shadow, scene, text, names, labels, borders, gridlines, panels or extra people. Every row has eight complete figures, not seven or nine. Four consecutive figures form one genuine FOUR-POSE sequence, individually drawn DIFFERENT bodily poses; no cloned complete body across cells. Source limbs, tail, cape and equipment stay complete.

ROW1 col1-4 INTRO: four distinct calm preparation/readiness poses with reference equipment safe. Col5-8 OUTRO: four distinct calm lowering/settling/turning poses, no attack.
ROW2 col1-4 ROUND VICTORY: four character-appropriate restrained acknowledgments. Col5-8 ROUND DEFEAT: four distinct catching-breath/kneeling/low-stamina poses, non-graphic.
ROW3 col1-4 FINALE: four individually drawn decisive-action poses, not an execution. Shoot/cast ONLY from the actual held barrel, staff head, or mechanical palm. The THIRD drawing (column2 zero-based) is the sole release/contact picture, with a tiny ATTACHED source-colour accent; first two drawings show no detached shot, beam or muzzle flash, and fourth is lowered/recovery without a flash. Do not draw long rays or disconnected projectiles. Col5-8 VICTORY: four distinct final restrained winning poses; do not duplicate the round-victory drawings.
ROW4 col1-4 DEFEAT: four distinct exhausted low/crouched or kneeling poses retaining full body and equipment; no dismemberment. Col5-8 SUPER: four individually drawn Railgun d’Uzi poses. Shoot/cast ONLY from the actual held barrel, staff head, or mechanical palm. The THIRD drawing (column2 zero-based) is the sole release/contact picture, with a tiny ATTACHED source-colour accent; first two drawings show no detached shot, beam or muzzle flash, and fourth is lowered/recovery without a flash. Do not draw long rays or disconnected projectiles. These are not copies of the finale row.
ROW5 col1-4 IDLE: four different relaxed breathing shifts. Col5-8 RUN: four genuine locomotion poses in the selected source anatomy; arms/legs/tails stay natural.
ROW6 col1-4 BASIC ACTION: four individually drawn actual equipped basic-action poses with the sole small release in the third drawing, no flash in the first, second or fourth. Col5-8 HIT REACTION: four clear non-graphic full-body recoil poses; no floating limbs or duplicate silhouettes.

All48 source poses must be present, separated and readable. No long detachedVFX, no tiny cropped half-body. Preserve full native equipment in every stage, including preparation and recovery.

Additional measured spacing requirement: keep each full figure compact, at most120pixels wide within an approximately181pixel square source cell, and keep at least20pixels transparent around the complete weapon/body. NO large crescent slash arcs, no large trails, smoke, sparks or effects between subjects. Tiny light edging on an actual held weapon is enough. Never join adjacent subjects with cloth, weapon or VFX.
